Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine
The Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine (LKCMedicine) trains doctors who put patients at the centre of their exemplary care. The School, which offers both undergraduate and graduate programmes, is named after local philanthropist Tan Sri Dato Lee Kong Chian. Established in 2010 by Nanyang Technological University, Singapore in partnership with Imperial College London, LKCMedicine aims to be a model for innovative medical education and a centre for transformative research. The School’s primary clinical partner is the National Healthcare Group, a leader in public healthcare recognised for the quality of its medical expertise, facilities and teaching.
The School turned a new chapter in its young history and transitioned to an NTU Medical School in 2024, ahead of the 2028 successful conclusion of the NTU-Imperial partnership to set up a Joint Medical School. In August 2024, we welcomed our first intake of the NTU MBBS programme, that has been recently enhanced to include themes like precision medicine and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare, with an expanded scope in the medical humanities. Graduates from the five-year undergraduate medical degree programme will have a strong understanding of the scientific basis of medicine, with an emphasis on technology, data science and the humanities.

Bachelor of Medicine & Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS)
The Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery degree (MBBS) is awarded by NTU Singapore.
Graduate Programmes
LKCMedicine offers graduate programmes that cater to healthcare professionals seeking to advance their expertise across fields such as research, palliative care, AI in medicine, sports medicine, and cardiovascular care, providing a flexible and comprehensive approach to professional development.
Short Course
Sports Medicine Theory Course
The Sports Medicine Theory Course (SMTC) is for medical doctors who would like to have a fundamental understanding of sports medicine.
Short Course
Musculoskeletal (MSK) Ultrasound Course
The MSK Ultrasound course is designed for nurses and allied health professionals (AHPs) who are interested in expanding their skills in diagnosing and managing upper and lower limb pathologies.
Artificial Intelligence in Medicine
The Master of Science, Artificial Intelligence in Medicine is a cutting-edge programme designed to merge the realms of healthcare and AI seamlessly.
Office of AIME (AI-Enhanced Medical Education)
Through curriculum innovation, assessment enhancement and educational scholarship, the Office translates emerging AI technologies into practical, evidence based solutions that improve learning outcomes while maintaining high standards of quality and governance.

Be part of our Research
SG100K: A Landmark Study in Singapore's Health and Well-being
SG100K is a pioneering study with researchers and healthcare institutions in Singapore. We're recruiting 100,000+ diverse participants aged 30-84 to address critical disease questions in Singapore's multi-ethnic population.
Learn more
BIOCIS: Research that transforms Cognitive Health
BIOCIS aims to discover early dementia biomarkers in a diverse group of 1,500 Singaporean participants. Data such as cognitive assessments and blood markers, will be collected at baseline, with a 5-year follow-up. Join us in preventing dementia.
Learn more
TARIPH Patient Network: Patient-focused Research
Through TARIPH Patient Network to co-develop patient-focused research, the TARIPH Centre will work with patients and their caregivers closely with clinicians and researchers providing their voices to respiratory medicine research.
Learn more
Brain Bank Singapore
Brain Bank Singapore collects brain tissue from both healthy individuals and patients to support research on neurological diseases. In collaboration with LKCMedicine, NNI, NHG, and NUS, it aims to advance understanding and develop better treatments through ethically approved studies.
